title: CS2 World Bundle network record
description: One line of networks.jsonl (JSON Lines). A record carries geometry in exactly one of two forms: a ripped mesh (assetId + pos + rot) or a centerline fallback (centerline + width) the consumer extrudes itself.

id.description: Producer-local stable identifier (the ECS entity index). Unique within the bundle.

kind.description: 'segment' is a run of network between two nodes; 'node' is a junction / intersection.

assetId.description: Mesh form only. Resolves to <layers.networkMeshes><assetId>.glb. Network meshes are generated per segment, so this is usually unique rather than deduped.

pos.description: Mesh form only. World position in bundle-frame metres.

rot.description: Mesh form only. World rotation as a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w].

centerline.description: Fallback form only. Polyline of world-space points in bundle-frame metres, from start node to end node. At least 2 points; curved segments are tessellated by the producer.

width.description: Fallback form only. Total network width in metres, to be extruded symmetrically about the centerline.

startNode.description: 'id' of the node record at the start of this segment.

endNode.description: 'id' of the node record at the end of this segment.

attrs.description: Semantic attributes. Free-form: consumers must ignore unknown keys and must not require any key.

form.description: Vertical form of the network, which a consumer needs to decide on bridges, tunnels and terrain cutting.

width.description: Total width in metres. Also emitted in the mesh form, where the top-level 'width' is absent.

elevation.description: Height of the network above terrain, in metres. Negative under terrain. CS2 stores one per end, so this is their mean; prefer elevationStart / elevationEnd, which are what the game actually holds.

elevationStart.description: Height above terrain at the start node, in metres. Negative under terrain.

elevationEnd.description: Height above terrain at the end node, in metres. Negative under terrain. A segment whose two ends differ climbs, and is where a consumer has to bridge or cut.
